title: Actor–critic training showed a local reversal in model-size scaling
summary: In Craftax, a larger actor–critic model outperformed a smaller one at 10¹⁴ training FLOPs, fell behind at 3×10¹⁴ FLOPs, and regained its lead by 10¹⁵ FLOPs. The result shows a local departure from monotonic scaling for the tested policy models. The authors proposed a learning-dynamics explanation based on in-game achievements.
ai_technology: Actor–critic reinforcement learning; empirical compute scaling

evidence.tested: The experiment trained model sizes across compute levels and examined the crossover alongside achievement frequencies.
evidence.unknown: The crossover concerns the evaluated sizes, training setup and game environment. The proposed explanation is observational.
evidence.ai_role: Trained actor–critic policies at different sizes and budgets generated behavior traces used to test local compute scaling.
